reason: The cited evidence supports that active-learning MLIPs can achieve DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys (E1, E2), but neither passage addresses free-energy surfaces, anharmonicity, electron-vibration coupling, or fusion properties. The key premises about capturing these specific thermodynamic contributions and the predicted speedup are unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: MLIPs can be trained to DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys
Active learning efficiently generates training sets for specific systems/properties
MLIPs can capture anharmonic vibrational effects and electron-vibration coupling
MLIPs trained on solid and liquid configurations can reproduce free-energy surfaces near melting
MLIP-based free-energy calculations will be ~10x faster than explicit AIMD/TOR-TILD
